note: Frames carry no biggerStudy field in format.ts (FrameSchema is strict); each committee frame's bigger study is in its note as 'biggerStudy: ...' (as templates-b; requested). Every list is office-free, so any frame may use any list. A frame names no visitor unless it is an advisor's vanity paper: the rules give it the club's spokesperson, whose club the strip shows, so a frame need not name the petitioner. Edited by the comedy editor (edit-templates-a): 44 of 60 frames rewritten or tightened; file order is by joke shape, no two neighbours alike.

lists.title: Things a town has
lists.note: Grammar: one thing any town has (no office place), singular, with 'the', lower case, at most 20 characters; reads after 'by', 'on', 'make', 'test whether' and 'who owns'.

lists.title: Small ceremonies
lists.note: Grammar: a small public occasion named as an official event, 'the' + noun + -ing (or 'the first cup of tea'), lower case, at most 22 characters; reads after 'at', 'for' and 'hold'. Nothing in it is a vote, a parade or a person.

lists.title: Mild weather
lists.note: Grammar: a spell of picnic weather, never worse than a drizzle (no heat, storm, flood or drought), with 'a' or 'an', lower case, at most 22 characters; reads after 'during', 'for', 'book', 'order', 'against' and 'how ... affects'.

lists.title: Minor inventions
lists.note: Grammar: one small household invention, with 'a' or 'an', lower case, at most 24 characters; reads after 'fund', 'put', 'study whether', 'show' and 'license'. Harmless, and never a machine for anything on the closed list.

lists.title: Dignified titles
lists.note: Grammar: an invented honorary title, lower case, no article, at most 24 characters; reads after 'the title of', 'as', 'name ... ' and 'be'. Never a real rank (no lord, knight, sir, dame, warden, sheriff, inspector of police, chief inspector), never a religious or military title.
